Two upgrades for IndexBoard, please keep everything else as it is.

1. Front page shows real work. Add a "Featured boards" section near the top of the home page with board cards (title, short description, number of items and metrics, top 3 items, Open button). Pin our real board first: "Paper Repro Index" at /b/5dhum9j5h0. Below it, a "Recent boards" gallery of the latest published boards from the database (newest first, up to 9).

2. Create a board with AI. On the create page add a tab "Describe it" next to the existing editor and a tab "Templates":
- Describe it: one big text box where the user can type or paste anything, even messy notes, a pasted table, numbers from a paper, or just a sentence like "compare GPT, Claude and DeepSeek on coding, cost and speed". Button "Build board". The app calls the LLM gateway once with json_mode true and asks for the exact board JSON this app already uses (title, description, metrics with direction higher/lower is better and unit, items with scores and optional low/high interval, methodology text). If the text has no numbers, the AI makes a clearly labeled draft with placeholder values and a yellow note "Example values, replace with your own". Then open the result in the normal editor so the user can fix anything before publishing. Show a friendly message on HTTP 429.
- Templates: 4 one-click starters (LLM leaderboard, Paper reproduction, Product comparison, Class or team ranking), each filling the editor.

LLM gateway (already built, never put a key in the app): POST https://vzvyghmtsakixlhzzuol.supabase.co/functions/v1/agent-llm with {"app":"indexboard","visitor":"<random id in localStorage>","messages":[...],"json_mode":true,"max_tokens":3000}. Returns {"message":{"content":"..."},"usage":{...}}.

Keep English and Chinese for all new text, light and dark mode, and no horizontal scroll at 390px.

Both upgrades are in. Lint and the build pass, and a visual check of the home page passed. One limit: I sent one test request straight to your AI gateway and it replied in the format the app reads, but I didn't run "Build board" end to end through the app.

**Front page**
- **Featured boards:** sits right under the hero, with "Paper Repro Index" pinned first. Its card shows the title, short description, number of items and metrics, the top 3 items with scores, and an Open button.
- **Recent boards:** a gallery of up to 9 of the newest published boards from the database, newest first. The pinned board isn't repeated there. It shows a loading state, a retry button if loading fails, and an empty-state message with a "Create a board" button.
- **If the pinned board doesn't load:** its card shows only the "Paper Repro Index" title with an Open link. The card fills in only once that board is found in the database the app is connected to, which may be the case only after publishing.

**Create page: Editor, Describe it, Templates**
- **Describe it:**
  - A big text box with two example prompts, a character counter and a "Build board" button.
  - It makes one request to your AI gateway with JSON mode on. A random visitor id is kept in the browser, and no key is in the app.
  - The prompt asks for the exact board format: metrics with units and higher/lower-is-better, items with optional intervals and run counts, the headline and cost metrics, and methodology.
  - The result opens in the normal editor for checking before publishing.
  - If the text has no numbers, the editor shows a yellow note: "Example values, replace with your own".
  - An HTTP 429 shows a friendly "too many requests, wait a minute" message. Network failures and replies that can't be read get clear errors too.
- **Templates:** four one-click starters (LLM leaderboard, Paper reproduction, Product comparison, Class or team ranking). Each fills the editor with metrics, placeholder values with intervals, and methodology, and shows the same yellow placeholder note.

All new text is in English and Chinese, follows light and dark mode, and stays within a 390px width. The new tabs appear only when creating a board, not when editing one. Everything else works as before.

You can try it in the App Viewer, then click Publish to deploy.

# Project Summary
IndexBoard helps AI researchers, students, and teams turn model, tool, or method evaluation results into shareable leaderboards. Authors can enter scores and uncertainty intervals, describe their methodology, publish a read-only board, and retain a private edit key. The app supports English and Chinese, system light/dark themes, charts, print, and JSON exports.

# Project Module Description
- **Board authoring:** Create or edit boards with a title, description, methodology, and metric results. Enter data in a table, paste JSON/CSV, or start from an example.
- **Leaderboard and analysis:** View metric charts with interval whiskers, a score-versus-cost scatter plot, model rankings, and methodology. Overlapping intervals are identified as statistical ties; rankings without intervals are marked provisional.
- **Sharing and access:** Store boards in Atoms Cloud. Public links are read-only; edits require a private key. Boards can be created without login.
- **Localization and display:** Switch between English and Chinese; light/dark mode follows system preference.
- **Export:** Print a board, copy charts as images or download them, and download or re-import board data as JSON.
- **Supporting services:** Backend modules provide authentication, database access, storage, settings, health checks, and AI hub integrations.

# Directory Tree
```text
.
├── DESIGN.md                         # Product design and architecture notes
├── app/
│   ├── start_app_v2.sh                # Application startup helper
│   ├── backend/
│   │   ├── core/                      # Configuration, auth, database, telemetry
│   │   ├── dependencies/              # Shared API dependencies
│   │   ├── models/                    # Database models
│   │   ├── routers/                   # HTTP API endpoints
│   │   ├── schemas/                   # API request/response schemas
│   │   ├── services/                  # Board and supporting business logic
│   │   ├── data_models/               # Board data definition
│   │   ├── alembic/                   # Database migrations
│   │   ├── skills_docs/                # Atoms Cloud integration guides
│   │   ├── main.py                    # Backend application entry point
│   │   └── lambda_handler.py          # Serverless handler
│   └── frontend/
│       ├── src/pages/                 # Home, editor, board, print, and blog pages
│       ├── src/components/             # Board, blog, and shared UI components
│       ├── src/lib/                   # API clients, board logic, i18n, utilities
│       ├── prerender/                  # Blog prerendering and sitemap utilities
│       ├── plugins/                    # Development safeguards and tests
│       ├── public/                     # Static assets and crawler directives
│       ├── package.json                # Frontend dependencies and scripts
│       └── vite.config.ts              # Vite configuration
```

# File Description Inventory
- `DESIGN.md` — Product design and implementation notes.
- `app/backend/main.py` — Configures and launches the API application.
- `app/backend/routers/` — Board, authentication, user, settings, storage, health, and AI hub endpoints.
- `app/backend/services/` — Board persistence and logic, authentication, storage, payment, user, and mock-data services.
- `app/backend/models/` and `schemas/` — Database entities and API data contracts.
- `app/backend/core/` — Application configuration, authentication, database setup, enums, encryption, environment handling, and telemetry.
- `app/backend/alembic/` — Alembic configuration and database migration history.
- `app/backend/skills_docs/` — Integration guidance for AI capabilities, custom APIs, object storage, and the web SDK.
- `app/frontend/src/pages/` — Main IndexBoard workflows, authentication callbacks, print view, and blog pages.
- `app/frontend/src/components/board/` — Leaderboard layout, charts, model table, and methodology view.
- `app/frontend/src/components/blog/` — Blog article presentation and markdown rendering.
- `app/frontend/src/components/ui/` — Reusable interface primitives.
- `app/frontend/src/lib/` — Board data and API helpers, general API clients, configuration, and translations.
- `app/frontend/prerender/` — Blog route, page, and sitemap prerendering.
- `app/frontend/plugins/` — React HMR and web SDK entity-update guards with tests.
- `app/frontend/package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, `tailwind.config.ts` — Frontend scripts, build tooling, and styling configuration.
- `app/start_app_v2.sh` — Application startup helper.

# Technology Stack
- **Frontend:** React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and reusable UI components.
- **Backend:** Python and FastAPI, with SQLAlchemy and Alembic for database access and migrations.
- **Charts:** Inline SVG charts implemented in the frontend.
- **Cloud services:** Atoms Cloud database and supporting SDK/API integrations.
- **Testing and quality:** ESLint, Playwright configuration, and plugin tests.

# Usage
- Install backend dependencies from `app/backend` with `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
- Install frontend dependencies from `app/frontend` with `npm install`.
- Run frontend linting from `app/frontend` with `npm run lint`.
- Start the frontend development server with `npm run dev`; create a production build with `npm run build`.
- Run the backend using `app/start_app_v2.sh`, or from `app/backend` with the configured ASGI server.
- Apply database migrations from `app/backend` with `alembic upgrade head`.
- Configure the required Atoms Cloud and database settings before running the application.
